evals.name: Registration form plan with React and Zod
evals.prompt: Quiero planificar un formulario de registro de usuarios para mi app en React. Usamos react-hook-form con Zod para validación. Los campos son: nombre completo (texto, obligatorio), email (email, obligatorio), contraseña (password, obligatorio, mínimo 8 caracteres), confirmar contraseña (password, obligatorio, debe coincidir con contraseña), y aceptar términos (checkbox, obligatorio). Al enviar se hace POST a /api/auth/register. Dame el plan antes de implementar.
evals.expected_output: A structured implementation plan in Spanish covering all fields, validation rules, architecture with react-hook-form and Zod, submission flow, and ordered implementation steps — without any code implementation

assertions.text: The response includes a table or list of all 5 fields: nombre completo, email, contraseña, confirmar contraseña, and aceptar términos
The plan mentions the cross-field validation rule that confirmar contraseña must match contraseña
The plan references react-hook-form and Zod as the libraries to use
The plan includes a submission flow section that references the POST /api/auth/register endpoint
The response includes a list of ordered implementation steps (not code, but actionable tasks)
The response does not include actual code implementation (no JSX, TypeScript, or function definitions)

evals.name: Contact form plan with missing stack info
evals.prompt: Need a plan for a contact form on our marketing site. Fields: full name, company email, phone (optional), subject (dropdown: Sales, Support, Partnership), and message (textarea). Form should submit to our CRM via a webhook. Haven't decided on the framework yet.
evals.expected_output: The skill should ask for the missing stack/framework information before delivering a full plan, or deliver a plan with clearly marked assumptions about the stack

assertions.text: The response either asks the user about the framework/stack or explicitly marks the stack choice as an assumption
The response mentions or lists the fields: full name, company email, phone, subject, and message
The response acknowledges that phone is optional and treats it differently from required fields
The response mentions the webhook submission as the form's send mechanism

evals.name: Checkout address form plan with i18n and a11y requirements
evals.prompt: Planifica un formulario de dirección de envío para un checkout en Angular. Usamos Reactive Forms y Ngx-Translate para i18n. Campos: calle (texto, obligatorio), número exterior (texto, obligatorio), número interior (texto, opcional), colonia (texto, obligatorio), ciudad (texto, obligatorio), estado (select con lista de estados de México, obligatorio), código postal (numérico 5 dígitos, obligatorio). El formulario debe ser accesible (WCAG 2.1 AA) y soportar español e inglés. Al guardar se llama a PUT /api/orders/{id}/address.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive plan in Spanish covering all 7 address fields, Angular Reactive Forms architecture, Ngx-Translate integration points, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility requirements, and the PUT endpoint submission flow

assertions.text: The plan covers all 7 fields: calle, número exterior, número interior, colonia, ciudad, estado, and código postal
The plan includes a section on accessibility (a11y) mentioning WCAG, aria attributes, or keyboard navigation
The plan references i18n or internationalization and mentions Ngx-Translate or translation keys
The plan specifies the PUT /api/orders/{id}/address endpoint as the submission target
The plan includes validation rules for código postal (5 numeric digits)
The response is written in Spanish
